title: Fill the AM-GM TODO: derive the Maclaurin step from Newton's log-concavity
problemStatement: The gallery file Proofs/AmgmInequalityOQ02.lean (Maclaurin Inequalities) carries two independent axiom declarations: newton_log_concavity (Newton's inequality (e_k/C(n,k))^2 >= (e_{k-1}/C(n,k-1))(e_{k+1}/C(n,k+1))) and maclaurin_step (M_k >= M_{k+1}). These are NOT logically independent: the Maclaurin step is a classical consequence of Newton's log-concavity. Goal: replace the maclaurin_step axiom with a formal Lean proof derived from newton_log_concavity, reducing the assumption set.
knownResults: Mathlib (checked 2026-06) has NEITHER Newton's inequalities NOR Maclaurin's inequality; no esymm log-concavity lemma exists.
Newton's log-concavity itself needs the real-rootedness / Rolle machinery and is a >1000-line build; it stays axiomatized.
The Maclaurin step is derivable from Newton via a discrete log-concavity / prefix-mean argument.

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: maclaurin_step derived from newton_log_concavity for strictly positive inputs (committed, build-unverified: Docker + Aristotle infra both down this session).
builtItems: Proofs/MaclaurinStepFromNewton.lean: maclaurin_core — p_{k+1}^k <= p_k^{k+1} by induction on k using only Nat-powers (the key reduction; avoids logs and infinite products).
Proofs/MaclaurinStepFromNewton.lean: rpow_cross — root-extraction lemma b^s<=a^t => b^(1/t)<=a^(1/s) for positive reals/naturals.
Proofs/MaclaurinStepFromNewton.lean: maclaurin_step_pos — M_{k+1}<=M_k for strictly positive inputs, from newton_log_concavity ALONE.
insights: Clean induction: with p_k = e_k/C(n,k) and p_0 = 1, Newton p_k^2 >= p_{k-1} p_{k+1} gives S(k): p_{k+1}^k <= p_k^{k+1} from S(k-1) directly. The inductive step is the multiplicative chain (p_{k-1} p_{k+1})^k <= (p_k^2)^k = p_k^{k-1} p_k^{k+1} <= p_{k-1}^k p_k^{k+1}, then cancel p_{k-1}^k > 0. This needs ONLY natural-number powers — no logarithms, no products over Finset.range.
Concavity intuition: a_j = log p_j is concave with a_0 = 0, so a_j/j is decreasing, i.e. M_k = exp(a_k/k) is decreasing. The Nat-power form sidesteps the log entirely.
Root extraction M_k >= M_{k+1} <=> p_k^{k+1} >= p_{k+1}^k by raising to the k(k+1) power (rpow monotonicity); proven as rpow_cross.

Positivity is essential: the ratio/cancellation argument needs p_j > 0, which holds for strictly positive inputs (each e_j > 0 for j <= n). The fully general non-negative case additionally needs a 'zeros form a suffix' lemma (if p_{k+1}=0 then M_{k+1}=0<=M_k; if p_{k+1}>0 then no earlier p_j vanishes, by Newton).
mathlibGaps: No Newton's inequality / elementary-symmetric log-concavity in Mathlib (would need real-rootedness via Rolle on the derivative of prod (t + x_i)).
No Maclaurin inequality chain in Mathlib.
